title: Sell Mineral Rights in Lakes of the North, MI
primaryKeyword: sell mineral rights lakes of the north mi
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Lakes of the North, MI
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Lakes of the North, Antrim County? Planned-community land with older Antrim Shale history underneath. Get a real evaluation.
heroLead: Lakes of the North is a planned recreational community built decades after the farmland underneath it was already leased for Antrim Shale gas, which is exactly why mineral ownership here rarely matches who owns the lots today.
intro: Lakes of the North is a large private recreational development in southern Antrim County, built out starting in the 1970s with man-made lakes, golf, and thousands of platted lots. The land it sits on was farm and forest ground before development, and mineral rights under that ground were commonly leased and, in places, drilled during the Antrim Shale boom of the late 1980s and 1990s, well before the current subdivision existed.

sections.heading: Why development here disconnected surface from minerals
paragraphs: When a large tract gets platted into a recreational development like Lakes of the North, the developer typically doesn't sell mineral rights along with each individual lot, it's common for those rights to have been reserved by the developer, a prior landowner, or split off entirely before development ever happened. That means owning a lot here tells you very little about whether you also own any minerals underneath it.

If you've received a small royalty check tied to land in this area but don't recall ever leasing anything yourself, it's likely connected to an interest that predates the development and simply passed down or got sold separately from your specific lot.

sections.heading: What that older interest is worth now
paragraphs: Where Antrim Shale wells were drilled on this ground before or during development, they're now decades into a mature, low-decline stage, meaning modest, steady production rather than anything resembling early boom-year numbers. We check current statements and activity before quoting anything, since not every parcel in this large development sits over an actual producing well.

faqs.question: If I own a lot at Lakes of the North, do I own the minerals under it?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. Mineral rights on much of this land were reserved or sold separately before the recreational development was built. Check your deed's mineral language to be sure.

faqs.question: Was this area part of the Antrim Shale boom before the development existed?
faqs.answer: Yes, the underlying farm and forest land in this part of Antrim County saw drilling activity during the 1980s and 1990s, before much of the current subdivision was built out.

faqs.question: How do I trace the mineral ownership history for land in this development?
faqs.answer: The Antrim County register of deeds in Bellaire holds the recorded deeds and leases predating the development, which is where the original mineral severance, if any, would show up.
